sections.content:
104,520 people

were counted on the census as "financial accounts managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Financial accounts managers manage client accounts or departments within financial institutions (such as banks and insurance companies) or manage a variety of financial accounts within other organisations.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "financial accounts managers", 15% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "financial accounts managers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "financial accounts managers" included:

  • production, factory and assembly supervisors
  • managers in storage and warehousing
  • aircraft pilots and air traffic controllers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "financial accounts managers" there were more women than men (55.9% compared with 44.1%).

This means "financial accounts managers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 44.1% and women made up 55.9% of "financial accounts managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "financial accounts managers" included:

  • newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors
  • business, research and administrative professionals (other)
  • catering and bar managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "financial accounts managers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "financial accounts managers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "financial accounts managers", 6.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (83.7% compared with 16.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.9%) than self-employed (3.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wandsworth, this is in the same region of London.
